I understand the goal.

The weekly automation should:

- Scan the previous 7 days across Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Cursor.
- Cover every repository and worktree.
- Group subagent transcripts under their parent session.
- Identify real user corrections, excluding approvals, quoted transcripts, forwarded prompts, automation noise, and tool output.
- Use separate subagents to inspect each agent store.
- Consolidate repeated patterns across sessions.
- Trace each correction to the nearest applicable `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, plus the personal or project skill active for that work.
- Recommend the smallest patch to the single best owner.
- Include session evidence, why existing guidance failed, the proposed diff, confidence, and how future runs will measure improvement.
- Avoid creating guidance for one-off mistakes or measurement errors.

There is already an older Agent Retro pipeline, but it only covers Codex and Claude and has known false-positive problems. I would extend the current `ce-sessions` / `ce-improve-skills` path, add OpenCode support, and schedule the improved loop for Sunday at 7:00 PM Pacific.

One question before I build it:

Should the automation only draft targeted patches for you to review, or may it automatically edit high-confidence guidance?

I recommend proposals only. Nothing changes until you approve it.
